title: Out of Support, Not Out of Reach: In-Context Learning with Unsupported Instructions and Composed Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2610.23528v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In-Context Learning (ICL) enables pretrained LLMs to adapt to downstream tasks from a small set of input-output demonstrations, without parameter updates. Yet existing theory primarily explains ICL as identifying a latent task already represented in pretraining, leaving unclear whether ICL can succeed when either the instruction or the target task falls outside the pretraining support. We develop a theoretical framework under mild assumptions that separates these two forms of distribution shift. For target tasks represented in pretraining, we show that demonstrations can identify the task and reduce sensitivity to pretrain-supported prompt templates as their number increases. For an unsupported instruction, we show that under a fixed model-induced reference extension, demonstration evidence can dominate an $N$-independent instruction shift while preserving the exponential identification rate. tldr: 该论文建立了理论框架，证明上下文学习即使在指令或目标任务超出预训练支持范围时仍能成功，示例证据足以克服指令分布偏移并保持指数级的任务识别速率。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a theoretical framework proving that in-context learning can succeed even when instructions or target tasks fall outside the pretraining support, with demonstration evidence capable of overcoming instruction distribution shifts while preserving exponential task identification rates.
